heroHeadline: CDMX World Cup Countdown: AICM at 90%, Airbnb Registry Launched, Azteca Structural Concerns
heroSubtitle: With 18 days to the FIFA World Cup opening match (June 11), Mexico City is in infrastructure overdrive: AICM's $500M Phase 1 renovation is 90% complete with a May 30 deadline, the Parque Elevado Tlalpan opens May 31, and the Brugada government launched a mandatory Airbnb/Booking registry (May 22) to prevent price gouging across 30,000+ short-term rentals. An ANTAC mega-march of 6,000–10,000 truckers and farmers shut down Paseo de la Reforma on May 20 demanding highway security. The Mexico Peace Index 2026 confirmed CDMX homicides are at their lowest level since 2022 — down 7% in January–April 2026 — though the city paradoxically ranked among states with greatest peace deterioration due to rising extortion and disappearances. Estadio Azteca faces unresolved Wi-Fi failures and concrete fragment safety concerns 19 days before the tournament opens.
footerNote: Data sourced from official CDMX government reports (Gobierno CDMX, SSC, SACMEX, SEMOVI, CAMe, CONAGUA), INEGI, Fiscalía CDMX, Congreso CDMX, NASA, La Jornada, El Universal, Proceso, Milenio, Infobae México, N+, El Financiero, Reuters, AP, and institutional analyses from UNAM, IMCO, México Evalúa, and the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP).
